glosses: to kill by causing such bloodloss, to bleed out
to bleed to death, to bleed out
An instance of exsanguination or of major blood loss.

examples.text: There are shootings, stabbings, car wrecks, falls and other accidents that can create a fatal bleed out situation.

glosses: An instance of any system or item that loses its necessary components, such as a machine and its fuel or a company and its money.
To die due to excess bloodloss; to bleed to death.

examples.text: But we never got to take the shot I'd been trained to take, that beautiful single shot that takes out a man's head, or the gutshot—Chris Kyle's favorite—that allows him to bleed out and die a little slower, maybe think about all the ways he might have lived a different and better life.

glosses: To kill by causing such bloodloss.

examples.text: Most slang begins in small communities, but some words bleed out into wider society over time.
